title: Higher journal fees are associated with more citations, but price is not a quality score

report.originalQuestion: How are article processing charges associated with journal citation measures, quartiles, and curated journal lists?

source.label: OpenAlex Sources API: journals with recorded APC

metricDefinitions.label: APC list price (USD)
metricDefinitions.definition: Current advertised journal APC converted to USD by OpenAlex; zero denotes a recorded no-fee price.

metricDefinitions.label: 2-year mean citedness
metricDefinitions.definition: OpenAlex citation-impact convenience metric using citations in the prior year to works from the two years before that.

metricDefinitions.label: h-index
metricDefinitions.definition: Largest h such that at least h works from the journal have at least h citations in OpenAlex.

metricDefinitions.label: OpenAlex field-adjusted quartile
metricDefinitions.definition: Quartile of 2-year mean citedness within the journal's dominant OpenAlex field; Q1 is the top 25%.
metricDefinitions.formula: descending percentile rank of two_year_mean_citedness within dominant_field

evidenceFlow.title: OpenAlex Sources API
evidenceFlow.detail: Cursor-paged every source with type=journal and a recorded APC in USD, including USD 0 and positive values. Selected journal identity, APC, summary citation statistics, source-list membership, OA flags, and topics.

evidenceFlow.title: Analysis
evidenceFlow.detail: Deduplicated on OpenAlex source ID; no duplicates were removed. Descriptive statistics use all recorded APC values.

caveats: APC is the current advertised list price converted to USD, not the amount an author paid.
OpenAlex APC coverage is selective and is thinner for hybrid journals.
Associations are descriptive and do not identify a causal effect of price on quality.
OpenAlex-derived quartiles are not Scopus/SCImago or Journal Citation Reports quartiles.
